person.name: Emmy Noether
person.summary: Amalie Emmy Noether was a German mathematician who fundamentally transformed abstract algebra and proved Noether's theorems linking symmetries to conservation laws in physics. A leading figure at Göttingen, she developed deep theories of rings, fields, and algebras, and later taught in the United States at Bryn Mawr College while conducting research at the Institute for Advanced Study.

events.title: Birth of Emmy Noether
events.description: Amalie Emmy Noether was born to mathematician Max Noether and Ida Amalia Kaufmann in Erlangen, Bavaria, into a Jewish family.

events.title: Passes Realgymnasium graduation exam in Nuremberg
events.description: Despite restrictions on women in higher education, Noether passed the graduation exam at a Realgymnasium, enabling her to continue advanced study.

events.title: Formally enrolls in mathematics at the University of Erlangen
events.description: After auditing courses and facing institutional barriers, Noether officially reentered the University of Erlangen–Nuremberg and committed to studying mathematics.

locations.name_historic: University of Erlangen–Nuremberg, Erlangen, Bavaria, Germany

events.title: Doctorate awarded under Paul Gordan
events.description: Noether earned her Ph.D. summa cum laude with a dissertation on invariants for ternary biquadratic forms under the supervision of Paul Gordan.

locations.name_historic: University of Erlangen–Nuremberg, Erlangen, Bavaria, Germany

events.title: Unpaid lecturer and researcher at Erlangen
events.description: Noether worked without pay at Erlangen's Mathematical Institute, occasionally substituting for her father and publishing on invariants, while women were largely excluded from academic posts.

events.date_note: She left for Göttingen in late April 1915.
events.title: Moves to Göttingen at Hilbert and Klein's invitation
events.description: Invited by David Hilbert and Felix Klein, Noether moved to the University of Göttingen. Faculty opposition initially prevented her from holding an official, paid position.

locations.name_historic: University of Göttingen, Göttingen, Prussia, Germany

events.date_note: Approximately two weeks after her move to Göttingen.
events.title: Death of her mother, Ida Amalia Noether
events.description: Soon after arriving in Göttingen, Noether returned to Erlangen when her mother died suddenly, adding personal hardship to an already difficult professional transition.

events.title: Noether's theorem presented in Göttingen
events.description: Felix Klein presented Noether's paper 'Invariante Variationsprobleme' to the Royal Society of Sciences at Göttingen, establishing the profound link between continuous symmetries and conservation laws.

events.title: Habilitation approved; becomes Privatdozent at Göttingen
events.description: Following the German Revolution’s reforms, Noether completed her habilitation and was recognized as a Privatdozent, with her first lectures listed under her own name that autumn.

events.title: Publishes 'Idealtheorie in Ringbereichen'
events.description: In a landmark paper, Noether developed the abstract theory of ideals in commutative rings, formalizing the ascending chain condition; structures satisfying it are now called Noetherian.

events.title: B. L. van der Waerden joins Noether's circle
events.description: Dutch mathematician Bartel Leendert van der Waerden collaborated closely with Noether in Göttingen; her ideas shaped the second volume of his 1931 textbook 'Moderne Algebra'.

events.title: Begins third epoch: work on noncommutative algebras
events.description: Noether focused on noncommutative algebras, hypercomplex numbers, and unifying group representation theory with modules and ideals, while influencing many students and colleagues.

events.date_note: ICM Zürich took place in early September 1932.
events.title: Plenary address at the 1932 International Congress of Mathematicians
events.description: By the time of her plenary lecture at the ICM in Zürich, Noether's stature as a leading algebraist was recognized internationally.

events.date_note: She moved later in 1933 after dismissal under Nazi policies; month approximate.
events.title: Dismissed by Nazi law; relocates to Bryn Mawr and lectures at IAS
events.description: Following the Nazi purge of Jewish academics, Noether left Göttingen for a faculty position at Bryn Mawr College and concurrently lectured and conducted research at the Institute for Advanced Study.

events.title: Death in Bryn Mawr, Pennsylvania
events.description: Emmy Noether died in the United States while on the faculty at Bryn Mawr College, closing a career that reshaped modern algebra and influenced physics.
